orchestrator-selected under standing stakeholder authority

The selected product is `md-fence-count`, a small deterministic CLI for developers, documentation maintainers, and CI authors who need a machine-readable count of Markdown fenced code blocks without installing a renderer or relying on parser-specific behavior.

The problem is that simple text searches miscount fences when marker type, indentation, opening length, closing length, info strings, unclosed blocks, or fence-like block content differ. Full Markdown renderers also introduce behavior outside this bounded need. The product goal is one documented counting rule with byte-stable JSON, explicit resource limits, strict input handling, and no network or configuration dependency.

The essential workflow is: a caller invokes `md-fence-count` with no arguments, supplies one document on standard input, checks exit status, and consumes one compact JSON object from standard output on success or standard error on failure. It reads at most 1,048,577 bytes to distinguish the inclusive 1,048,576-byte limit, checks size before strict UTF-8 decoding, parses LF and CRLF lines, applies only the declared fence state machine, and returns the count. It does not read paths or publish during normal use.

An opening fence has zero to three leading ASCII spaces followed by at least three identical backticks or at least three identical tildes. A backtick opening fence's info string cannot contain a backtick; a tilde opening fence may have any UTF-8 info string. A closing fence has zero to three leading ASCII spaces, the opener's marker, at least the opener's marker length, and only ASCII spaces or tabs afterward. Four or more leading spaces prevent opening or closing. A shorter fence, the other marker, or a candidate closer with non-whitespace trailing text remains content. Fence-like lines inside an open block never open nested blocks and close only when they satisfy that block's closing rule. An unclosed opener counts once through end of input. Lone CR is ordinary text.

Success is measurable by black-box cases that cover backtick and tilde blocks, zero through four leading spaces, exact and longer closers, short and wrong-marker closers, valid and invalid info strings, unclosed blocks, embedded fence-like lines, empty input, LF, CRLF, and lone CR. Repeating an invocation with the same bytes must produce the same exit status and exact output bytes. Every supported input writes exactly `{"codeFenceCount":N}` plus LF to standard output, writes no standard error, and exits 0. Inputs over the byte limit, invalid in-limit UTF-8, and any argument respectively return stable `INPUT_TOO_LARGE`, `INVALID_UTF8`, and `INVALID_USAGE` JSON errors on standard error only, with exit status 2. Boundary tests must accept exactly 1,048,576 bytes and reject 1,048,577 bytes.

Non-goals are Markdown rendering, code extraction, language inference, file or directory traversal, options, nested fenced blocks, streaming output, configuration, network access, mutation, and CommonMark behavior not explicitly listed. Product-wide constraints are Node.js execution in the controlled pilot environment, no runtime dependencies that require external services, the inclusive raw-byte limit, strict UTF-8, bounded memory proportional to the declared input limit, stable JSON key order and messages, and publication only to `https://github.com/taylorrowser/mdlm-markdown-code-fence-count-pilot` after lifecycle authorization.
